blocks.task_summary: Find probability that the fourth of four employees is the only one working >40 hours per week.
method_path: Recognise independent trials with p = P(T > 40) from (a)
Multiply (1 − p)³ × p for exactly the fourth being the first success

evidence.basis: attempt to multiply four independent probabilities using their P(T > 40) and P(T < 40) (M1); (1−p)³·p (A1); 0.0443 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: (i) Find P(T < 55 | T > 40) using conditional probability. (ii) Find P(exactly 5 of 10 from the >40h group work <55h) using binomial distribution.
method_path: Compute P(40 < T < 55) / P(T > 40) using normal distribution
(ii) Recognise binomial model X ~ B(10, p) with p from (i)

evidence.basis: (i) recognizing conditional probability (M1); P(40 < T < 55)/P(T > 40) (A1); 0.461944…/0.574136… (A1); = 0.805 (A1). (ii) recognizing binomial probability (M1); n = 10 and p = 0.804… (A1); P(X = 5) = 0.0242 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: Given P(a ≤ T ≤ b) = 0.904 and P(T > b) = 2P(T < a), find a (maximum part-time hours) using probability-sum-to-one and inverse normal.
method_path: Let P(T < a) = x, then P(T > b) = 2x
Find a using inverse normal: P(T < a) = 0.032 with μ = 42, σ = 10.7
accepted_alternatives: Express P(T < a) = (1/3)(1 − P(a ≤ T ≤ b)) = (1/3)(1 − 0.904) = 0.032 directly, then use inverse normal to find a ≈ 22.2

evidence.basis: recognition that probabilities sum to 1 (M1); expressing the three regions in one variable (M1) → x + 0.904 + 2x = 1; P(T < a) = 0.032 (A1); a = 22.2 (A1). Alternative: P(T < a) = (1/3)(1 − P(a ≤ T ≤ b)) = 0.032 (A1).
